Often overshadowed by Thai, Chinese, and Japanese food—cuisines that in fact borrowed from it—Vietnamese cuisine is finally being recognized. From Hanoi to the Mekong, Franco-Vietnamese chef Mai Mai reveals a legacy of balance and depth, from fragrant broths and fresh herbs to vibrant street fare, now honored in Michelin's first all-Vietnamese guide.

Founded by Trotsky in 1918 amid total war, the Red Army abandoned its democratic ideals to crush civil uprisings. Fearing its power, Stalin launched the Great Terror of 1937-38, purging its officers. Weakened, the army nearly collapsed when Germany invaded in 1941. Only Zhukov's leadership, fierce resistance, and Allied support carried it to Berlin, uncovering death camps along the way.
